name: IZOLYATSIA
known: Wikipedia names Lyubov Mikhailova, daughter of the last Soviet director of an insulation materials plant on that territory, as founder.
IZONE's profits went to IZOLYATSIA projects; its main income came from leasing premises, which has ended (Promote Ukraine, Marta Barandiy, interview with the development director, 8 November 2021).

name: Mystetskyi Arsenal
known: In July 2013 the director had Volodymyr Kuznetsov's painting painted black and Vasyl Tsagolov's work excluded; artists called a boycott. 2025 visitors: 53,870.

name: National Art Museum of Ukraine
known: First director: Mykola Biliashivsky.
The current director listed is Yulia Lytvynets (Wikipedia).
State museum under the Ministry of Culture; its income and spending plans must be agreed with the ministry (former director Mariia Zadorozhna, LB.ua interview, 2015).
In October 2012 staff sent an open letter demanding the removal of acting director Tatiana Mironova; art workers backed it with a statement and petition.

name: National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War
PinchukArtCentre
known: Founded by Victor Pinchuk, who consolidated his philanthropy under the Victor Pinchuk Foundation in 2006.
The centre site names Pinchuk as founder.
No records of its own: its founder's Victor Pinchuk Foundation posts annual reports from 2009 to 2018; the centre lists staff, no funders or board.

name: Mariupol Drama Theatre
known: Reopened 28 December 2025 with a gala concert attended by Denis Pushilin, the Moscow-backed head of Donetsk region, and St Petersburg governor Alexander Beglov (AP via PBS).

name: Cove Park
known: Named buildings: the Jacobs Building takes the founders' name.

Programme: residencies for artists, plus the engagement programme Collective Home: Community, Creativity & Action in Argyll, which director Alexia Holt discussed in The Lochside Press (16 March 2026).

name: Catalyst Arts
known: Artist-run gallery at 6 Joys Entry in Belfast city centre, run by volunteers as a non-profit, members-based organisation: the committee is responsible to members, and directors serve limited terms (Catalyst Arts).
Founded in 1993 by MFA graduates of the Belfast School of Art as an artist-led project, led by joint co-directors who each served a two-year term.
Current directors: Niamh Birch, Lauren Morrisson, Nicola Kenny and Tori Clarkson.

name: Spike Island
known: Hauser & Wirth: platinum Gallery Supporter, and supports three Engagement Fellowships for South West curators running 2025 to 2028, each with financial support and mentorship (Spike Island).
Individual patrons by tier: Tony Ades (gold), Phil Toy (silver) and David Greene (bronze) in the Director's Circle;

name: CCA Derry~Londonderry
known: Catherine Hemelryk is named as Director in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports.

Jerwood Developing Artists Fund funded the expanded Supports Programme from January 2023, and the Jerwood Foundation funded New Curating after the Jerwood Curatorial Accelerator (annual report to March 2024).

name: CCA Glasgow (Centre for Contemporary Arts)
known: Grew out of the Third Eye Centre, a multimedia arts centre opened in 1974 and founded by the Scottish Arts Council.

name: The Royal Standard
known: Run by directors who serve unpaid two-year terms (The Double Negative, C.

name: Auto Italia South East
known: Edward Gillman was director from 2019 to 2024.
Maggie Matić has been director since May 2024.
